capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Wikipedia: long-wheelbase ID. Buzz (North America) gross 91 kWh / net 85.

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: VW Newsroom (LWB premiere): 85 kWh net battery. Wikipedia agrees (91 gross / 85 net).

chemistry.notes: Estimated: EVSpecs lists the ID. Buzz long-wheelbase 91 kWh gross / 86 usable pack as Lithium Nickel Manganese Cobalt (NMC); the US 2025 car carries the same 91 kWh pack (Wikipedia, VW 85 net). Community database, not a VW statement.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: the ID. Buzz is built on VW's MEB platform, which Guide Auto lists at 400 V for the ID.4 82 kWh pack (the Buzz pack is larger, 91 kWh); no page states the Buzz voltage. Platform-level estimate.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: vw.com says that on "most 2024 and newer Volkswagen EV models" the car starts preheating the battery automatically when an active route to a DC fast charger is set (a Battery Optimization toggle exists in Charging Settings, which is not shown to be a manual start button). The page does not list models and the ID. Buzz is not named; the 2025 ID. Buzz is assumed included.

dc_max_kw.notes: vw.com: "Charge from 10% to 80% in 26 minutes with 200kw DC fast charging". Wikipedia gives 170 kW for the short-wheelbase pack only.

ac_max_kw.notes: vw.com: 11 kW Level 2 charger (240 V), up to about 9 hours from empty. Canada not separately sourced (same car).

published_10_80_min.notes: vw.com: 10-80 % in 26 minutes at 200 kW DC.
